Handle re-authorization callbacks triggered by scope changes at any time

approval.cost: A 'review and listing fee' exists: 'click Submit app for Review to pay the review and listing fee and submit the app. Test the app before submitting it to avoid paying additional review fees.' The fee AMOUNT is not stated in the docs read. Resubmission economics: 'If the app is resubmitted within 30 days and shows progress, no additional fee will apply. After 30 days, a new submission and fee are required.' Whether BigCommerce charges revenue share or ongoing listing fees after approval is not mentioned in the pages read
approval.trigger: Yes, for distribution beyond your own stores. 'Apps that aren't approved for distribution through the App Marketplace can only be installed on stores owned by the same email address as the developer portal account's email address.' An unapproved app is a draft app: installable only on stores registered to the same email as your Developer Portal account, and only the store owner can install it. There is no separate 'private/unlisted multi-store' tier documented; reaching other merchants' stores requires Marketplace approval, and a BigCommerce partnership is 'required to publish apps to marketplace'. Review is triggered by clicking 'Publish app...' in the Dev Portal and then 'Submit app for Review' (paying the review and listing fee). 'The Marketplace team reviews all app submissions and tests apps to verify they meet App Marketplace listing standards': all listing fields completed; support resources in-app; branding rules (no competitor references; same app name in submission and content); all callback URLs over HTTPS; apps 'must be multi-user enabled'; apps 'should be single-click and use OAuth flow to authenticate'; tokens stored 'against the store hash, not the user's email address'; V3 endpoints preferred over V2; apps creating orders must set external_source to the app's ID; payment apps 'must pass a PCI Compliance review by BigCommerce's security team and provide both a PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance and a data flow diagram', and 'We have paused all new externally built payment integrations for our publicly available BigCommerce Marketplace' (payment submissions must be pre-approved). Apps accessing the Checkout Content scope get an additional security assessment; 'Modify All' scope configurations 'will not be approved for public listing'. Pre-approval cap: structural, not numeric (same-email stores only). Response obligations: 'Partners must respond within 30 days of receiving feedback'; 'Non-responses result in app rejection due to inactivity'.
approval.wait: Not stated (no overall review-duration figure; listing edits 'can take up to 24 hours to appear on the App Marketplace' after approval)

blockers.detail: 'There is no way to manually revoke or force-regenerate app-level API account access tokens.' A stored token is invalidated the next time the merchant opens the app after (a) you change the app's OAuth scopes, or (b) the store owner's email address changes; the merchant is prompted to re-accept, the previous access_token becomes invalid, and you receive a fresh auth callback. Dev Portal scope edits 'are effective immediately for all app users'.
blockers.howToClear: Handle re-authorization callbacks as a normal event at any time, not just at install, and avoid casual scope changes.
blockers.title: Token invalidation is event-driven, not manual

blockers.detail: Unapproved apps install only on same-email stores, and only the store owner can install apps. A third-party developer cannot install a draft app on a client's store with delegated credentials; distribution to clients requires Marketplace approval (or the client manually creating a store-level API account instead).
blockers.howToClear: Plan the Marketplace submission (and partnership) before promising client installs.
blockers.title: Draft-app ownership trap

blockers.detail: The merchant 'accepts the app's OAuth scope permissions. The OAuth consent view presented to the merchant requires them to approve all the scopes to install the app; at this time, merchants cannot pick and choose scopes.' Over-scoping at install time is an install-conversion risk, and post-approval 'Modify All' scope sets are unapprovable.
blockers.howToClear: Request the minimum scope set that the product genuinely needs.
blockers.title: All-or-nothing consent

alternatives: Store-level API account (generated by the merchant in one store's control panel under Settings > Store-level API accounts; includes 'a static access token that does not change'; the docs' capability table lists this for 'Manual connection between a third-party app and a store'. Simpler, but per-store manual setup and no install/uninstall lifecycle callbacks; note 'You can't change store-level access tokens or OAuth scopes' after creation)
Account-level API account (for the GraphQL Account API; one token covering all stores under a merchant account)
flavor.recommended: A single-click app using the BigCommerce-initiated grant code authorization flow (a modified OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant)
flavor.why: The object is an app registered in the BigCommerce Developer Portal (build.bigcommerce.com). Creating an app also creates an app-level API account with a client_id and client_secret: 'The client ID and client secret will never change.' The merchant installs from the App Marketplace (or a direct installation link), approves scopes, BigCommerce calls your GET /auth callback with a temporary code, and you POST it to login.bigcommerce.com/oauth2/token to receive a permanent, per-store access_token, used in the X-Auth-Token header against api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/... Each application generates 'a unique access token for every store that installs the app'.

humanMust: Get the prerequisites: a BigCommerce sandbox store (required to test app installation), a Developer Portal account (required to register apps), and a BigCommerce partnership (required to publish apps to the Marketplace)
Create the app in the Dev Portal and generate credentials
Configure the Auth, Load, and Uninstall callback URLs (publicly available, fully qualified, TLS/SSL in production) and set OAuth scopes on the app profile
Complete the listing and submit for Marketplace approval (paying the review and listing fee)
name: BigCommerce
nuances: 'Deleting an app also deletes its API account... you can't recover the app or its API account'; for a deleted app 'there is no way to recover the client ID or client secret'. Store-level accounts are similar: deletion 'cannot be undone' and a deleted account 'cannot be recovered'.

'Some resources are only accessible to the API account that created them. These include webhooks, metafields, and scripts': revoking or replacing an account orphans them. And: 'An attacker can use your client_secret to both sign and decrypt JWTs sent between you and BigCommerce'.

Your app must respond to the auth callback with styled/branded HTML rendered in the control-panel iframe; a blank response leaves the merchant 'looking at a blank screen'. 'It's a best practice to request and receive an access_token before responding to the auth callback.'

Scopes are set per app profile in the Dev Portal, not requested per install, and payment apps are effectively closed: 'BigCommerce only accepts pre-approved new payment gateway app submissions' and new externally built payment integrations for the public Marketplace are paused.
prerequisites: A BigCommerce sandbox store for testing installation
A Developer Portal account; a partnership for Marketplace publishing
Callback URLs that are publicly available, fully qualified, and served over TLS/SSL

steps.detail: Dev Portal > Create app > name it > Generate Credentials; the dialog shows the app's Client ID and Client Secret (they never change). Prerequisites: a sandbox store to test installation and a Developer Portal account to register apps.

links.label: Managing Apps in the Developer Portal

steps.title: Create the app; generate credentials

steps.detail: In the App information tab, set the callback URLs: Auth (requested when the store owner clicks install), Load (app launch), Uninstall, and optionally a Remove-user callback; enable multiple users if needed. In the Scopes tab, toggle the required scopes, Save changes, Confirm new scopes (scopes are set per app profile, not requested per install).
steps.title: Configure callbacks and scopes

steps.detail: The merchant clicks Install in the App Marketplace or follows a direct installation link and approves all the scopes (no partial consent). BigCommerce calls GET /auth?code=...&scope=...&context=stores/{store_hash}&account_uuid=... POST the code to login.bigcommerce.com/oauth2/token with client_id, client_secret, code, context, scope, grant_type 'authorization_code', and redirect_uri identical to the registered auth callback. Save the returned access_token, scope, user, owner, context, and account_uuid, keyed by store hash.
steps.title: Merchant installs; exchange the code

steps.detail: Call api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/... with the X-Auth-Token header. Tokens do not expire and there is no refresh flow. Implement Load (verify signed_payload_jwt, issue a session) and Uninstall (teardown) callbacks, and handle fresh /auth callbacks whenever scopes change or the store owner's email changes.
steps.title: Call the API with the permanent token

steps.detail: Complete all listing fields (Case Studies and Videos optional), click 'Publish app...' then 'Submit app for Review' and pay the review and listing fee (amount not stated). Respond to Marketplace team feedback within 30 days; resubmission within 30 days with progress carries no additional fee, after 30 days a new submission and fee are required. Approved listing edits 'can take up to 24 hours to appear on the App Marketplace'.
steps.title: Submit for Marketplace approval

tagline: A real install OAuth flow that issues permanent per-store tokens (no expiry, no refresh), but distribution is the gate: unapproved draft apps install only on stores owned by your own email address, and reaching other merchants requires Marketplace approval and a partnership.
